text:
Maya: quick sync — we need to finalize reranker payload gating before next week's dedup rollout
Liam: +1, what's the current ask?
Maya: two things: 1) enforce candidate_count limit per tenant at edge (so heavy long-list apps can't blow up batch sizes), 2) deterministic fallback to cheaper model when latency budget exceeded
Sasha: for (1) do we want hard-reject or soft-truncate with a telemetry tag?
Maya: prefer soft-truncate + metric so product teams don't get 429s unexpectedly. tag = rerank.truncated=true
Liam: sounds good. what should default candidate_count be? 100? 200?
Devon: 100 default, but allow tenant override up to 1000 with dedicated quota. default avoids worst-case batches
Sasha: ok. about (2) — model fallback: should the client receive the fallback model id in response? need to show provenance in console and for audits
Maya: yes include model_provenance field in the envelope. minimal: model_id, fallback_reason (e.g., latency_budget, capacity_constrained), and score_version
Liam: score format question — teams want either raw_logit or normalized_confidence. do we support both in envelope or one canonical?
Devon: my vote: canonical "score" is normalized [0..1] confidence. add optional raw_logit for debugging behind feature flag. saves ambiguity for billing and ranking logic
Sasha: agreed, but we should add a "score_type" enum so consumers know which score they read
Maya: drafting API patch: response.envelope = { scores: [...], model_provenance: {...}, score_type: "normalized" } and optional raw_logits array if requested with ?debug_logits=true
Liam: telemetry: emit per-request model_switch boolean, truncated_count, and latency_bucket. also histogram of post-fallback latency
Sasha: console UX: show model switch events in timeline for a tenant + percent of requests falling back last 24h. canary-bot should annotate rollout periods
canary-bot: new canary window for reranker v2 starts 2026-04-01T15:00Z — annotate on console if enable_canary=true
Devon: rollout policy: canary -> gradual traffic ramp -> auto-fallback threshold at 5% error/latency regressions. ops notified at 2%
Maya: one more: quota accounting. do we bill by input candidate_count or by output tokens? rerank should count candidate_units = max(1, log2(candidate_count)) ?
Liam: billing team prefers linear units to keep it transparent. propose candidate_unit = ceil(candidate_count / 50). simpler for customers
Sasha: implement dual telemetry: report raw_candidate_count and billed_candidate_units so console shows both
Maya: ok I'll create the PR: api contract + migration notes + console mockups. tagging @Liam @Sasha for review.
Liam: thanks, will review today
Sasha: will skim and drop inline comments
Devon: I'll add quota hooks and e2e tests for fallback flow
Maya: perfect. leaving UX and billing follow-ups in a separate thread after merge :thumbsup:
